o: Our God, thank You for the life You give me and for this new morning. I acknowledge that everything I am and everything I have comes from Your generous hand: my strength, my mind, my family and the opportunities opening before me today. Thank You, because You never leave me empty-handed.

Lord, sometimes I compare myself to others and feel that what I have is little. Sometimes I hide for fear of making a mistake, like one who keeps a treasure under the ground. Today I want to change this. Give me the courage to use joyfully what You have given me, great or small. Teach me to be faithful in the simple tasks of this day: in my relationships with my family, in my work and in the words I speak.

Take from me laziness, envy and the fear that paralyzes. Help me serve others with humility and not seek applause. May every act of kindness I do today be done as for You. Keep my steps, my mind and my heart, and as evening falls, may I feel in my soul Your smile of approval. In Jesus' name, amen.
h: Jesus told a parable about a man who, before setting out on a long journey, called his servants and entrusted his property to them. To one he gave five talents, to another two and to another one, to each according to his ability. Then he went away. No one received the same, but all received a real responsibility.

The one who had received five talents went at once and put them to work, and he gained five more talents. The one who had received two did the same and gained two more. But the one who had received only one went and dug in the ground and hid his master's money. He did not squander it; he simply did nothing with it out of fear.

After a long time, the master returned and settled accounts with his servants. To the first two, he said exactly the same words: “Well done, good and faithful servant; you have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much; enter into the joy of your master.” Notice that the one who had two received the same praise as the one who had five. God measures not only what we produce, but the faithfulness with which we use what he has given us.

The servant who had hidden his talent, on the other hand, said that he had been afraid, and that this was why he kept it. His master called him a wicked and slothful servant. His problem was not having little, but the mistaken picture he had of his master and the fear that had paralyzed him.
Through this parable, Jesus teaches us that every person has received something from God and that one day we will give account with joy, not terror, whether we have been faithful.
m.c: May the Lord give you today a courageous heart to do the good that is before you, even if it seems small. Do not walk in fear: the one who called you is faithful and goes with you. Go out with confidence, for his approval is worth more than any applause.
m: The parable of the talents is often read with great abilities in mind, but its message begins in everyday life. The master gave each one “according to his ability,” that is, without demanding more of him than he could do. God does not ask you to be someone else or to have what you do not have. He asks you for faithfulness with what is in your hands today: your time, your voice, your home, your skills, your attention.

There is a moving detail in the text. To the one who had gained two and to the one who had gained five, the master says the same thing: “You have been faithful over a little.” For God, the little is not a small thing. A call to encourage someone, a job done with honesty, a patience that does not give up: all of this counts when it is done from the heart. Here there is no competition, for the Lord does not compare his children with one another.

The third servant warns us about fear. He hid what he had because he thought ill of his master. Often we stop doing good because we think we will not be good enough, or that we will make mistakes. But the God of Jesus is generous and patient. You can take the step with the peace of knowing that you are not working for a tyrant, but for a Father who rejoices with you.

For today, choose one concrete thing you are putting off out of fear or laziness, and do it before the end of the morning. It might be reconciling with someone, visiting a person who is alone, starting a difficult task or devoting ten minutes to prayer. Offer it to the Lord and believe that he multiplies what is done in faith.

t.t: Do Not Be Afraid, Only Believe
o: Good Father, I come to the end of this day with gratitude. Thank You for keeping me at every hour and for the signs of Your love that sometimes go unnoticed: a smile, an open door, food on the table, a kind word. Everything comes from Your faithful hand.

Lord, today too there was news that frightened me and situations I could not change. There are moments when it seems it is already too late for my dreams, for my family or for my health. But You say: “Do not fear, only believe.” I now give You my fears, my losses and my extinguished hopes. Take my hand as You took that young girl's, and restore life to what is weary in me.

Forgive me if, today, I let fear speak louder than Your word. Take care of the sick, of those who weep and of those who keep watch tonight beside a bed. Give them Your consolation and Your peace. Grant me quiet sleep and may I rise tomorrow with the certainty that You are at work even when I do not see. Thank You for everything, Lord. In Jesus' name, amen.
h: One day, while Jesus was by the sea, one of the leaders of the synagogue, named Jairus, came to him. He fell at his feet and begged him earnestly: “My little daughter is at the point of death. Come and lay your hands on her, so that she may be made well and live.” Jesus went with him, and many people followed and pressed around him.

On the way, Jesus stopped to attend to a woman who had suffered for twelve years. For Jairus, every minute counted. While Jesus was still speaking, people from the synagogue leader's house arrived with terrible news: “Your daughter is dead. Why trouble the Teacher any further?”

Jesus heard what they said and told Jairus: “Do not fear, only believe.” He allowed no one to follow him except Peter, James and John. When he arrived at the house, he saw a great commotion, people weeping and wailing loudly. He told them the child was not dead but sleeping, and some laughed at him. Then he put everyone out, took with him the child's father and mother and his three disciples, and went in where the child was.

He took her by the hand and said to her: “Talitha cumi,” which means: “Little girl, I say to you, arise.” And immediately the girl got up and began to walk, for she was twelve years old. Those present were seized with great amazement. Jesus ordered that she be given something to eat.
Jairus received the worst news of his life and, right there, he heard the firmest word: “Do not fear, only believe.” No situation, however dark it seems, is beyond the reach of Jesus' hand.
t.c: Breathe deeply and let go of the day: what was good was a gift from God, and what was hard remains in his hands. The one who raised a young girl from her bed also cares for your night. Rest in peace, for the Lord's faithfulness is your shelter.
m: Jairus was about to see Jesus heal his daughter when the news came that it was already too late. Sometimes life puts us right there: when we think something still has a remedy, circumstances tell us it does not. At that moment, there are two voices. One says: “Trouble him no more.” The other, Jesus', says: “Do not fear, only believe.” Today it is worth asking ourselves which of the two we listen to more.

Notice that Jesus did not scold Jairus or explain much to him. He gave him a command full of love and stayed at his side. He walked with him to the house. This teaches us that faith is not a force you produce by effort, but trust in a person who walks with you. When your faith is weak, do not stay far from Jesus; draw nearer to him.

There is also a lesson in the gesture: Jesus took the girl by the hand. God does not act only from afar; he draws near, touches and lifts up. What seems lost in your life, whether a relationship, a hope or your spirits, is not far from his touch. And after raising her up, Jesus asked that she be given something to eat: he cares about the small and practical things of our lives.

Tonight, before sleeping, name in prayer what you find hard to believe will change. Say aloud: “Lord, you say not to fear; I take your hand.” Then write one sentence of gratitude for something God has already done today. You will sleep with more peace when you remember that the last word belongs to Jesus, not to the bad news.
